items.title: SpaceX seeks about $40B of debt, led by Apollo, to buy Nvidia chips, FT reports
items.summary: The Financial Times reported, and Reuters and Bloomberg relayed, that SpaceX is looking to raise about $40 billion to fund a large Nvidia chip order: roughly $10 billion of bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt. Apollo is expected to lead and place the debt with investors, and SpaceX is reportedly in talks with PIMCO. Bloomberg describes the talks as early and says they could end without a deal; Benzinga says closing is expected in 2027.
items.why_it_matters: It shows AI capex moving into investment-grade credit markets at a size few issuers can match, and ties SpaceX (which absorbed xAI) to Nvidia supply for Colossus and orbital compute.

items.title: Marvell lifts FY2028 revenue target to about $20B and sets FY2031 range of $70-90B at investor day
items.summary: At its Oct 6 investor day in New York, Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue target from $18B to about $20B, above the $18.2B consensus cited by coverage, and set a first fiscal 2031 range of $70-90B. It lifted its FY2029 custom-silicon target to above $12B and cited a $400B AI addressable market by 2030. Coverage ties the targets to an August Google agreement with warrants linked to up to $120B of cumulative custom-chip orders; the stock rose over 7% intraday.
items.why_it_matters: It reads as a bet that hyperscaler custom ASIC and optical interconnect demand will outgrow merchant GPUs, a direct challenge to Broadcom, with a hyperscaler-warrant structure that ties customer orders to Marvell equity.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for prompts under 100K, matching GPT-6 Luna
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, its small model, with API pricing of $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens (down from $1/$5 on Haiku 4.5) and $0.50/$2.50 above that. Anthropic reports 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset; 15.7% for Haiku 4.5) and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (0% for Haiku 4.5), and puts average savings near 75% after a tokenizer change that uses slightly more tokens per task. The model also adds adjustable effort levels.
items.why_it_matters: The base rate matches OpenAI's smallest model, GPT-6 Luna, so the small-model tier is now a price fight. Cheap computer-use and agentic-coding capability at this level lowers the cost of running sub-agent fleets, though the 100K-token step-up and tokenizer change blunt the headline cut for long-context agent loops.

items.title: Memphis council delays data-center moratorium vote to Oct 20 for a second time, amid protest and a lobby fistfight
items.summary: The Memphis City Council voted 7-5 on Oct 6 to push its vote on a data-center moratorium, along with related data-center ordinances, to Oct 20; it had already slipped from Sept 15. Protesters erupted, a fight broke out in the lobby, police cleared the chamber and the meeting was recessed. The council also agreed to a Thursday working session on the remaining issues.
items.why_it_matters: The pause would not cover xAI's existing Colossus sites but would freeze new approvals, making Memphis a test of local pushback against Musk's expanding AI footprint.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model for on-device search
items.summary: Google DeepMind published EmbeddingGemma 2, an open-weight embedding model that maps text, images, video and audio into one shared vector space for search and organisation on local devices. One report puts it at about 740 million parameters. It was first posted on October 6.
items.why_it_matters: An open, small multimodal embedder lets developers build private on-device retrieval without calling a hosted API such as Gemini Embedding 2. It extends the Gemma line into retrieval, a core piece of agent memory stacks.

items.title: Nous Research confirms $90M Series B at $1.5B valuation, launches Hermes agents for businesses
items.summary: TechCrunch reports the Hermes open-source agent developer raised $90M in a Series B at a $1.5B valuation, led by Robot Ventures with Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung and 1789 Capital participating. Total funding is now $158M. It confirms July reporting that a round of at least $75M was being finalised, and the company is launching agents for business users.
items.why_it_matters: Investors, including Nvidia and Samsung, are funding open-source agent frameworks that compete with OpenClaw-style local agents.
